slots.note: Carbon-fibre filled and ABRASIVE. This printer's nozzle is stainless steel (profiles/printer-p1s.json, read from telemetry), which PLA-CF wears. A DFM rule pairing abrasive filament against nozzle material is a Phase 4 candidate; until it exists this note is the warning.

The external spool holder. PC and PA are hygroscopic enough that the AMS is a liability and they run from here (PRD 15.7); what is physically on it right now is a generic PLA (tray_info_idx GFL99). An external spool has no AMS slot and mapping to one raises - it is fed by hand, and it is not 'slot 4'.

notes.this_file_is_a_claim: It is checked against the printer before every dispatch by printer.reconcile_ams (ADR-16), and a material mismatch in a slot the print uses is a BLOCKER. It shipped through two phases disagreeing with the AMS in four of five slots, and nothing noticed, because nothing had ever asked the printer. tests/fixtures/filaments_drifted_s16.json is that version, frozen as a regression.
notes.frame_materials_not_loaded: Neither Bambu PAHT-CF (PA-CF) nor Bambu TPU 95A (TPU), the fpv frame's materials, is loaded as of 2026-10-07. PAHT-CF is AMS-compatible per Bambu and would take a bay; TPU 95A is not (too soft for the feed channel, Bambu filament guide) and goes on the external spool. Until a spool is loaded and this inventory re-read from telemetry, ams_mapping(['PA-CF']) and ams_mapping(['TPU']) raise 'not loaded', and profiles/calibration.json's PAHT-CF_bambu and TPU-95A_bambu stay unmeasured (seanrobertwright/fpv #5).
notes.no_abs_is_loaded: ABS is not in the AMS. slicer.ams_mapping(['ABS']) now raises 'not loaded', which is correct and is why profiles/calibration.json's ABS_generic stays a published default with "measured": null.
